name: employee-training
description: Chapter 3: hire an employee, obtain a licence no role starts with (driving.excavator) and a second skill the trainee lacks (geology) via real click-driven training, then complete a blast task. Courses grant new qualifications only (#1388); a held skill (a driller's blasting or driving.drill_rig) is never offered. #553: drill_hole is a queued, vehicle-gated action (a driller physically drives a drill_rig to each hole); drillers start with driving.drill_rig, so only a drill_rig purchase is needed. campaign start was replaced with new_game: a manually-bought vehicle spawns at grid centre, and new_game's 64x64x64 default halves the trip. Schools are placed apart: driving_center at (3,5), geology_lab at (5,15). drill_plan grid is 2x2 (4 holes): a single driller/drill_rig lands one hole roughly every 40-45 ticks door-to-door, so 9 holes risked the site's own cash burn (no income anywhere in this file). `event choose 0` follows tick blocks: idempotent no-op when nothing is pending.

steps.description: #553: cash bumped from the default $50,000 to cover the drill_rig ($35,000) on top of the original curriculum's driving_center/geology_lab/training costs, with headroom for the ~250-tick runway's payroll/vehicle upkeep (no income anywhere in this file) and one lawsuit event (observed: Aesthetic Pollution, $15,000, seed 42).

(#1203) #1203's arrival-gated training turned this file's fixed `tick N` pads into `wait_until` waits on real walk time, lengthening the runway (two schools' worth of walk-there-train-walk-back, plus the drilling grind) enough that the driller's own fatigue-driven wellBeing now bottoms out and ends in a worker revolt before the blast step. A site policy's revision only takes effect once applied (forceShiftRestIfNeededByPolicy, ForceShiftRest.ts), and this policy's own rest destination is any living_quarters tier or resting in place if none exists (dest.worthwhile) -- no living_quarters is ever built in this file, so this alone is what lets the crew take a proactive rest at all through the grind ahead. Left at SITE_POLICY_DEFAULT_THRESHOLD (60, no explicit fatigue: override, unlike tutorial-interactive.json's own #1151 fix at 75): the dedicated builder's own place_building work is protected mid-execution (PROTECTED_MID_EXECUTION_ACTION_TYPES) but not its walk there, and a threshold as aggressive as 75 sent it back for rest often enough that the blasting_academy build never landed inside this step's own 300-tick wait budget -- confirmed live. Applied before any training/build step so nothing above depends on which toolbar panel this leaves open (every later step already re-clicks its own panel explicitly).

#556: a dedicated builder — a `place_building` order needs an idle employee to walk over and do the work, and that must not be the driller trained below: with only one employee on site the build and the courses interleave, and a 20-tick course then does not finish inside the 20-tick block that asserts it did. Cheapest role (driver, $800); it does no driving here. It stays on the roster for the rest of the file — hireEmployee’s unionized roll (deterministic for seed 42) lands on this hire, and a unionized employee cannot be fired at all (`fireEmployee`, Employee.ts). Its own driving.truck starting qualification is why every qualificationCount below reads one higher than the driller’s own. No toolbar click here: the employees panel is already open from the hire above.
#553: without a drill_rig on site, drill_hole's vehicle gate (#550) never finds a free vehicle to claim -- the drill_plan below would sit queued forever.

Real UI training gap (parity with the deleted playtests/training.json, #479): driving.excavator belongs to no hiring role (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION), so a driving_center -- the only school that teaches it -- is the sole in-game path to ever holding it. Placed away from the drill grid below (20,20)-(23,23).

expect.note: Confirming placement only queues a construction site (#556) — the next step waits for it to actually land before training depends on a real school existing.

steps.description: Drive the driving_center site to completion (#556) — the driller (only employee on site) does the building work itself before returning to train.

Real click path: open the employee detail panel, confirm the excavator course is genuinely offered and clickable (#479's own concern -- "if this control is missing or disabled with a school standing, the licence belongs to nobody"), then enrol. (#1203) Enrolment sends the employee walking to the school rather than relocating them instantly -- trainingCount (trainingState !== null) stays 0 until they actually arrive and enter the building.

(#1203) The driller built this school itself just above, so it is standing right next to it -- but arrival is still a real walk, not a teleport, so this waits for trainingState to be promoted from pendingTrainingState on entry rather than assuming enrolment itself started the course.

(#1203) Replaces a fixed `tick 20` pad that assumed instant relocation. The course itself is exactly TRAINING_BASE_TICKS(20) * TRAINING_TIER_SPEED[1](1) = 20 ticks from arrival (the fee is the flat TRAINING_BASE_FEE, #1388), but arrival itself takes a variable number of walk ticks, so this waits for the course to actually land rather than guessing an offset from the enrol command.

expect.note: the excavator licence is genuinely obtained -- no role starts with it, so this is the only way anyone on the roster ever holds it One higher than the driller’s own count: the dedicated builder hired above brings its driving.truck starting qualification (#556).

steps.description: #553: idempotent -- a no-op ('No pending event or invalid option.') when nothing is pending, resolves one when a timer fired mid-tick-block. A bare `tick` refuses outright while an event is pending, so skipping this defensively stalls every tick step after it.

Second school: prove a skill the trainee lacks is obtainable via real clicks from a second school type. Courses grant new qualifications only (#1388) -- the driller already holds blasting and driving.drill_rig (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATIONS), so the course taught here is geology, which no driller starts with. #553: placed at (5,15), far enough from driving_center at (3,5) and the drill grid at (20,20)-(23,23) that the trainee is never stranded on another school's footprint.

expect.note: Confirming placement only queues a construction site (#556) — the next step waits for it to actually land before training depends on a real school existing.

steps.description: Drive the geology_lab site to completion (#556).

Chuck Miner holds no geology (a driller's ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATIONS are blasting and driving.drill_rig), so the geology course is offered; the same control as the excavator course above. A held skill would render a locked 'already qualified' row instead. (#1203) Enrolment sends the employee walking to the school rather than relocating them instantly -- trainingCount stays 0 until they actually arrive and enter the building.

(#1203) geology_lab sits at (5,15), a longer walk than the driving_center training above -- this waits for arrival and trainingState to be promoted from pendingTrainingState, rather than assuming enrolment itself started the course.

(#1203, #1388) The geology course is also TRAINING_BASE_TICKS(20) * TRAINING_TIER_SPEED[1](1) = 20 ticks from arrival; a pending event auto-resolves inside this wait (runWaitUntil/interaction-executor's own waitUntil loop).

expect.note: a new qualification is added (geology at Rookie): the driller's count rises by one. One higher than the driller's own count: the dedicated builder hired above brings its driving.truck and driving.excavator starting qualifications (#556).

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:3 depth:6 start:20,20
steps.description: #553: shrunk from the original rows:3 cols:3 (9 holes) to 2x2 (4 holes) -- confirming the grid queues 4 drill_hole PendingActions and pushes 4 PlannedHoles into plannedDrillHoles, none drilled yet, so holeCount stays 0 right after confirm. A single driller/drill_rig lands roughly one hole every 40-45 ticks door-to-door (walk to vehicle, drive, drill, return for the next); 9 holes risked the site's own cash burn (no income anywhere in this file) outrunning the plan.

expect.note: 2 rows x 2 cols = 4 holes ordered (ghosts), none drilled yet (#553)

steps.description: #1384: drilling time now scales with proficiency/fatigue/Living Quarters, so the old fixed 4x tick 40 pads no longer land the holes at a fixed tick. Wait on the condition instead.

expect.note: All 4 holes have landed — none lost, none left ordered forever.

steps.description: #554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.

#592: qualificationCount/proficiencyTotal dropped from 4/6 to 0/0 -- this file's only employee (Chuck Miner, the driller hired at step 1) dies in the `blast` step above (confirmed via direct trace: `alive:false` immediately after), and both fields are now computed over living employees only (issue #592 -- a dead employee's frozen qualifications used to permanently pollute this aggregate). With nobody left alive, both are genuinely 0 -- not a bug, the earlier `tick 32` step (qualificationCount:4) already proved the training landed before the blast.

expect.note: One higher than the driller’s own count: the dedicated builder hired above brings its driving.truck starting qualification (#556). proficiencyTotal 1, not 0: the dedicated builder hired at the top survives the blast that kills the driller, and keeps its driving.truck at Rookie (#556).
